findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items are unreachable when only a Grafana Prometheus rule is available
findings.body: The Pause menu item is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` and the Delete menu item is gated on `rulerRule` truthiness (lines 123 and 165). In the new 'no ruler calls in list view' flow (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons.V2 -> AlertRuleMenu), only `promRule` is passed and `rulerRule` is always `undefined`. The new Grafana-prom-based ability checks (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) correctly compute `canPause`/`canDelete` as true when the user has permission, but because the render conditions additionally require a non-null `rulerRule`, the Pause and Delete menu items never render in this code path even for fully permitted users. This silently removes the ability to pause or delete alert rules from the alert list view, which directly contradicts the goal of keeping these actions working while removing ruler API calls. This is confirmed by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx asserting the menu contains exactly 4 items (silence, copy-link, duplicate, export) even though delete permission was granted in that test's setup.

findings.title: Missing `key` prop when rendering GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterView
findings.body: When switching from the removed `GrafanaRuleLoader` (which had `key={key}`) to the new `GrafanaRuleListItem`, the `key` prop was dropped: `<GrafanaRuleListItem rule={rule} groupIdentifier={groupIdentifier} namespaceName={ruleWithOrigin.namespaceName} showLocation={true} />`. The sibling branches (`DataSourceRuleLoader`, `UnknownRuleListItem`) still pass `key={key}`. Since this is rendered inside an array (`rules.map(...)`), React will emit 'missing key' warnings and may misidentify/incorrectly reconcile list items (e.g. during incremental loading via infinite scroll), causing stale DOM state or unnecessary re-mounts for Grafana rule items in the filtered list.

findings.title: View link no longer includes `returnTo` query param
findings.body: The previous implementation (deleted `GrafanaRuleListItem` in `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) built the rule view URL with a `returnTo` parameter via `createReturnTo()`: `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view', { returnTo })`. The new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` builds the href as `createRelativeUrl('/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view')` without `returnTo`. This drops the 'navigate back to the list' context that was previously passed when a user clicked into a rule's detail view from the list, degrading back-navigation UX for all Grafana rules rendered through this component (used by both FilterView and GrafanaGroupLoader).

findings.title: Stray leftover comment '// duplicate' in useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities
findings.body: The line `const { isEditable, isRemovable, loading } = useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable(rule); // duplicate` contains a leftover inline comment that doesn't explain anything meaningful and appears to be a stray note from development (possibly meant to flag duplicated logic with `useIsRuleEditable`). It should either be removed or replaced with a clear explanation, since as written it is confusing to future maintainers.

findings.title: No test coverage for Pause or Delete menu items in the new ruler-free rule list flow
findings.body: The test 'should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked' grants `AccessControlAction.AlertingRuleDelete` (and others) but asserts only 4 menu items exist (silence, copy-link, duplicate, export) and never checks for Pause or Delete. Given that `AlertRuleMenu`'s Pause/Delete rendering depends on a `rulerRule` which is never supplied in this flow (see AlertRuleMenu.tsx finding), this test effectively documents the regression but does not call it out or assert that it is expected/intentional behavior, so a future reader could easily overlook that Delete/Pause silently never appear in this view.
